description: Provide the mathematical background for carrying out optimization associated with nature inspired techniques, and provide an introduction to the basic principles, techniques, and applications of nature inspired optimization techniques.

syllabus.title: Introduction to Algorithms
syllabus.body: Optimization, search for optimality, nature-inspired metaheuristics, analysis of optimization algorithms, parameter tuning and parameter control.

syllabus.title: Random Walks and Simulated Annealing
syllabus.body: Random variables, optimization as Markov chains, step sizes and search efficiency, modality and intermittent search strategy, importance of randomization, eagle strategy; simulated annealing: annealing and Boltzmann distribution, SA algorithm, basic convergence properties, stochastic tunneling.

syllabus.title: Evolutionary and Swarm Algorithms
syllabus.body: Genetic algorithms: role of genetic operators, choice of parameters, GA variants, convergence analysis; particle swarm optimization: swarm intelligence, PSO algorithm; firefly algorithms; cuckoo search: cuckoo breeding behavior.

syllabus.title: Advanced Topics
syllabus.body: A framework for self-tuning algorithms, handling constraints, multi-objective optimization, other and hybrid algorithms: ant algorithms, bee-inspired algorithms, differential evolution.

outcomes: Learn the mathematical basis as well as general principles of various nature-inspired optimization techniques and algorithms.
Understand and implement the concept of optimization techniques.
Develop familiarity with current research problems and research methods in this field.
textbooks: Xin-She Yang, Nature-Inspired Optimization Algorithms, Elsevier publications, First Edition, 2014.
referenceBooks: Nazmul Siddique, Hojjat Adeli, Nature-Inspired Computing Physics- and Chemistry-based Algorithms, First Edition, 2017.
